blocks.text: What an AI assistant for Zoom on Mac does during a call

Lazur lives in the notch at the top of your Mac screen. You hold ⌥⌘, which is Option plus Command, and ask in plain words. Let go when you finish. Lazur answers out loud, using what it sees on screen as context.

Lazur is not a plugin or add-in for Zoom. It does not click buttons, edit files, or operate other apps for you. You still mute, share, and record yourself. Lazur finds the right control and tells you what to press.
That split matters during a live call. Zoom's own controls stay in your hands. Lazur fills the gap when you cannot find a button, forget a shortcut, or need a sentence fast.
Five things Lazur does in a Zoom meeting

items: Explain what is on screen. Ask 'What does this message mean?' and Lazur reads the message and answers out loud.
Point at things. Ask 'Where is the mute button?' and Lazur draws a circle and a label around it on your screen.
Walk you through a feature. Ask 'How do I share one window?' and Lazur guides you one click at a time, waiting for each click.
Draft text at the cursor. Ask for a short reply, and Lazur types the draft where your cursor sits.
Dictate. Hold fn and speak. Lazur types clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app.

blocks.text: Zoom camera and echo problems on Mac, by the numbers

Zoom's own FAQ lists camera problems and echo among its common questions. The list includes 'Why isn't my camera working?' and 'Why is there an echo?' Those are the moments when a host needs an answer in seconds, not a help article open in a second window.

The wider research points the same way. Owl Labs' 2025 State of Hybrid Work report found that 77% of workers say they have lost time to technical difficulties in meetings. 76% cite audio echo or distortion. Those figures cover hybrid meetings in general, not Zoom alone.
Here is how the common Zoom questions map to what you can ask Lazur. Each row starts with the problem you hit, then the question to say out loud.

blocks.text: Zoom's FAQ answers these questions in general terms. Lazur answers them against the window you have open right now. That is the difference that matters mid-call.

blocks.title: Check the screen first
blocks.text: Lazur looks at your screen only while you hold the shortcut. Before you ask, close chat threads, client files, or notes that should stay private.
Zoom system requirements on Mac you should check first

Zoom's system requirements article lists macOS 10.15 or later as the minimum. It sets a dual-core 2 GHz CPU and 4 GB of RAM as the minimum hardware. It recommends a quad-core 2.5 GHz CPU and 16 GB of RAM.

A Mac at the minimum has less room for a busy call. Close heavy apps before you join, especially browsers with many tabs. Then check that the Zoom window is visible, since Lazur can only help with what it sees.

Keep the Zoom Workplace app current too. The most recent macOS release in Zoom's release notes is 7.2.5 (build 90525), dated October 31, 2026. Zoom's lifecycle policy sets 6.0.2 as the minimum Workplace version for macOS, enforced on November 7, 2026.
Lazur runs on macOS, on both Apple silicon and Intel Macs. It does not update Zoom for you, so check for updates before an important call.
Ask Lazur about your screen during a Zoom call

Hold ⌥⌘, speak, and release. A good question names the thing you see. Say 'the gray button under the video' or 'the message in the top corner.' Lazur uses your words and the screen together, so vague questions get vague answers.

Practice this before your first real call. Open a quiet document, hold ⌥⌘, and ask 'What is on my screen?' Listen to the answer. Then try a button question. You learn the timing once, away from the client.
A worked example: a screen share that shows the wrong window
You share your screen on a client call, and the room sees your desktop instead of the slide deck. You need to fix it without losing the flow of the meeting. Start by asking what the room sees.

items: Hold ⌥⌘ and ask 'Why can't they see my slides?' Lazur reads the screen and explains what it sees.
Ask 'Walk me through sharing one window.' Lazur guides you one click at a time.
Click the control Lazur points at, then wait for the next instruction before you move.
Keep each question short. Short questions return short, usable answers.

blocks.text: The whole fix takes less time than explaining it to the room. Stay with one step at a time, and do not rush ahead of Lazur's instructions.
What Lazur sends and stores during a meeting

Lazur listens and looks only while you hold the shortcut. Your audio and a screenshot go to AI providers so Lazur can answer. The audio and screenshot are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models.
Your meeting still contains what people say, so think before you ask about a client file. A question about one line of a contract shares more than you meant if the contract is open on screen.
Zoom keyboard shortcuts on Mac to learn first
Zoom's hot keys article lists the Mac shortcuts most people use. Some are faster than any question. Learn these first, since you use them in almost every call.

items: ⌘⇧A: mute or unmute
⌘⇧V: turn the camera on or off
⌘⇧S: start screen share
⌥Y: raise or lower your hand
⌘J: join a meeting
⌘D: schedule a meeting
⌘⇧R: start a local recording
⌘⇧C: start a cloud recording
⌘⇧P: pause a recording

blocks.text: Zoom lets you change these in its keyboard shortcut settings. If you change one, ask Lazur what the key does now. Lazur explains and points, but it does not press the key for you. Pressing it is your job.
Dictate and draft in the Zoom chat on Mac
Hold fn to dictate. Lazur turns your speech into clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app. That covers the Zoom chat box, a note you have open, or an email you start during the call.

Dictation is included with Lazur and is unlimited on both paid plans. Snippets help when you type the same thing often, such as a meeting link or a standard reply. A personal dictionary helps with names and product terms the speech engine gets wrong.

Draft with a question when you need words fast. Say 'Draft a reply that says I need a few more minutes.' Lazur types the draft at your cursor. Read it before you send, and press the send control yourself.
Dictated text can mishear a name, a figure, or a time. Read the line before you send it to the whole room.
Edge cases that catch people out in Zoom

items: Your speakers can feed the call. Lazur answers out loud through your Mac. If the speakers are loud and your microphone is on, the call may pick up the answer. Use headphones or mute before you ask.
Hidden windows stay hidden. Lazur answers from what is visible when you hold the keys, so bring the right window forward first.
Long questions get fuzzy answers. Ask one thing at a time.
Shortcuts can change. Zoom lets you edit them, so a key in this guide may not match your settings. Check your keyboard shortcut settings if a key does nothing.

blocks.text: Mistakes people make with an AI assistant in Zoom

items: Releasing the keys too early. Lazur only listens and looks while you hold ⌥⌘. Release before you finish, and the question gets cut short.
Asking about a window you cannot see. Bring the Zoom window forward first. Lazur can only help with what is on screen.
Expecting Lazur to click. It points and it guides. You do the clicking, one step at a time.
Trusting a draft without reading it. Dictation can mishear names and numbers, so check before you send.
Skipping your company rules. Some workplaces limit AI tools in meetings. Ask your admin first, especially for client calls.

blocks.text: Free Zoom meeting limits to plan around

Zoom's admin FAQ says free accounts allow up to 100 participants per meeting and 40-minute meetings. A paid Zoom Meetings license has no 40-minute limit. If a call runs long on a free account, the meeting ends at the cutoff.
Ask Lazur to set a timer a few minutes before the cutoff. Timers are one of the everyday actions Lazur handles. You can also ask it to add a Calendar event for the follow-up call.
Troubleshoot echo and camera issues during a Zoom call

Say your camera shows a blank box. Hold ⌥⌘ and ask why. Lazur reads the message on your screen, explains it out loud, and then guides each step in the camera settings. It waits for your click before it moves on.

For echo, start with the basics. Use headphones, and mute people who are not speaking. Echo often comes from a speaker feeding a microphone in the same room. Then ask Lazur to walk you through the audio settings.
If the fix does not work, say so. Ask Lazur what to check next. It answers from the screen you have, so tell it what you tried.
What to do before your next Zoom call

[Download Lazur](/download), open it once, and try a single question while a window is open. Then read the plans on the [pricing page](/pricing) before you commit. The app starts with a free trial that needs no credit card.
Start small. Ask about the mute button before a meeting that matters. Then try a dictated reply in a quiet chat. Give the hold timing a few tries before you rely on it.

faq.question: Is Lazur a Zoom plugin or add-in?
faq.answer: No. Lazur is not a plugin or add-in for Zoom or any other app. It is a voice assistant for the Mac that works in any app, including Zoom. It does not click buttons or operate Zoom for you.

faq.question: Can Lazur mute me or start my camera in Zoom?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons or operate other apps. It can tell you the shortcut, ⌘⇧A for mute or ⌘⇧V for the camera, and point at the button. You press the key or click yourself.

faq.question: Does Lazur work on Intel Macs?
faq.answer: Yes. Lazur runs on macOS, on both Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Zoom's Workplace app for macOS needs macOS 10.15 or later, according to Zoom's system requirements article.

faq.question: Does Lazur listen to my whole Zoom meeting?
faq.answer: No. Lazur listens and looks only while you hold the shortcut you use. Your audio and a screenshot go to AI providers to answer, and they are not stored.

faq.question: What is the Zoom shortcut to raise my hand on Mac?
faq.answer: Option+Y raises or lowers your hand, according to Zoom's hot keys article. You can change the shortcut in Zoom's keyboard shortcut settings if you prefer another key.

faq.question: Why is there an echo in my Zoom call on Mac?
faq.answer: Echo often comes from speakers feeding a microphone in the same room. Zoom's FAQ lists echo among its common questions. Ask Lazur to walk you through the audio settings one click at a time.

faq.question: Does a free Zoom account have a time limit?
faq.answer: Yes. Zoom's admin FAQ says free accounts allow 40-minute meetings and up to 100 participants per meeting. A paid Zoom Meetings license has no 40-minute limit.
